tiwanaku.name: Tiwanaku
tiwanaku.summary: A major pre-Columbian archaeological site in Bolivia near Lake Titicaca, home to an estimated 10,000 to 20,000 people around 800 CE, with monumental structures and megalithic stonework.

wari-empire.name: Wari Empire
wari-empire.summary: A political formation that emerged around 600 CE in Peru's Ayacucho Basin and expanded across much of coastal and highland Peru, lasting about 500 years until 1100 CE.

nazca-culture.name: Nazca culture
nazca-culture.summary: An archaeological culture that flourished from about 100 BC to 800 AD on Peru's southern coast, known for ceramics, textiles, geoglyphs, and underground aqueducts called puquios.

cerro-ba-l.name: Cerro Baúl
cerro-ba-l.summary: An ancient Wari political and ceremonial outpost on a terraced mountain in Peru, with remains of a brewery and ceremonial buildings that its own people later destroyed before abandoning it.

cahuachi.name: Cahuachi
cahuachi.summary: A major ceremonial center of the Nazca culture in coastal Peru, active from about 1 to 500 CE and thought to have been a pilgrimage site rather than a capital.

puquios.name: Puquios
puquios.summary: Ancient underground aqueducts that carry water long distances without evaporation loss in the dry coastal deserts of southern Peru and northern Chile, dozens of which still function today.

wari-culture.name: Wari culture
wari-culture.summary: A Middle Horizon civilization flourishing across the south-central Andes and coastal Peru from about 500 to 1000 AD, which at its height formed the Wari Empire centered near modern Ayacucho.

neltuma-pallida.name: Neltuma pallida
neltuma-pallida.summary: A thorny mesquite tree native to coastal Colombia, Ecuador and Peru, known as huarango or kiawe, valued for preventing river and wind erosion.

gate-of-the-sun.name: Gate of the Sun
gate-of-the-sun.summary: A monolithic stone gateway at Tiwanaku in Bolivia, carved by the Tiwanaku culture around AD 500–950 and decorated with carvings thought to have astronomical significance.

pumapunku.name: Pumapunku
pumapunku.summary: A 6th-century terraced platform mound near Tiwanaku, Bolivia, considered that site's most important structure besides Akapana, its foundation once supporting as many as eight stone gateways.

akapana.name: Akapana
akapana.summary: An artificial earthen platform mound at the Tiwanaku site in Bolivia, shaped like a half Andean cross, 257 meters wide and 16.5 meters tall, faced with stone blocks including carved puma and human heads.

moche-culture.name: Moche culture
moche-culture.summary: A civilization that flourished in northern Peru from about 100 to 800 CE, likely a group of autonomous polities sharing culture rather than a single empire, known for rich art and architecture.

alexei-vranich.name: Alexei Vranich
alexei-vranich.summary: American archaeologist specializing in pre-Columbian South America, whose current work focuses on the origins of the Inca Empire. He is a Fulbright Scholar and Dumbarton Oaks Harvard Fellow.

department-of-ayacucho.name: Ayacucho
department-of-ayacucho.summary: A department in the south-central Andes of Peru, called Huamanga until 1825; it was among the hardest-hit areas during the Shining Path guerrilla war of the 1980s.

joyce-marcus.name: Joyce Marcus
joyce-marcus.summary: American archaeologist and University of Michigan professor whose research focuses on the Zapotec, Maya and Andean civilizations, known for her 'Dynamic model' of social hierarchy.

moquegua.name: Moquegua
moquegua.summary: A city in southern Peru and capital of the Moquegua Department, located about 1,144 kilometers south of Lima.

periodization-of-pre-columbian-peru.name: Periodization of pre-Columbian Peru
periodization-of-pre-columbian-peru.summary: Archaeological periods for pre-Columbian Peru: the Middle Horizon (600–1000 CE) saw shared religious icons spread widely, while the Late Intermediate Period followed a major state's collapse.

paracas-culture.name: Paracas culture
paracas-culture.summary: An Andean society that existed roughly 800 to 100 BCE on Peru's south coast, known for irrigation skills and elaborate textiles; its Cavernas and Necropolis burial sites yielded richly decorated ceramics and cloth.

quipu.name: Quipu
quipu.summary: Knotted-cord record-keeping devices used by Andean cultures, especially the Inca, to store numbers and other data in a decimal positional system; they date back to at least the 1st millennium CE.

bernab-cobo.name: Bernabé Cobo
bernab-cobo.summary: A Spanish Jesuit missionary and writer (1582–1657) who spent 61 years in Spanish America and helped bring cinchona bark, source of quinine, to Europe.

sican-culture.name: Sicán culture
sican-culture.summary: Culture of Peru's north coast between about 750 and 1375 CE, also called Lambayeque culture. Named by archaeologist Izumi Shimada, it followed the Moche culture.

wari-archaeological-site.name: Wari (archaeological site)
wari-archaeological-site.summary: Archaeological site near Quinua in the Ayacucho Region of Peru, at about 2,600 to 2,900 metres elevation. It was the capital of the Wari Empire and one of ancient Peru's largest urban settlements.

viracochapampa.name: Viracochapampa
viracochapampa.summary: Archaeological site in Peru with the remains of a pre-Inca building complex, near Huamachuco in La Libertad region. It was one of the administrative centers of the Wari culture.

department-of-cajamarca.name: Cajamarca Department
department-of-cajamarca.summary: Department in northern Peru that borders Ecuador. Its capital, the city of Cajamarca, lies at 2,700 metres in the Andes, and part of its territory reaches into the Amazon rainforest.

aymara-people.name: Aymara people
aymara-people.summary: An Indigenous Andean people of about 2.3 million living mainly in Bolivia, Peru, Chile and Argentina, who came under Inca and then Spanish rule.

viracocha.name: Viracocha
viracocha.summary: Creator and supreme deity of pre-Inca and Inca mythology, said to have made the universe, sun, moon, stars and time, and to have ordered the building of Tiwanaku.

staff-god.name: Staff God
staff-god.summary: A recurring front-facing figure holding an object in each hand, a religious icon shared across pre-Columbian Peru, with its oldest known depiction dated to 2250 BCE.

amaru-mythology.name: Amaru
amaru-mythology.summary: A mythical double-headed serpent or dragon in Andean, especially Inca, mythology, representing infinity, knowledge and cosmic renewal and linking the earthly and spiritual worlds.

anadenanthera-colubrina.name: Anadenanthera colubrina
anadenanthera-colubrina.summary: A South American tree, also called vilca or huilco, growing 5 to 20 meters tall with mimosa-like leaves that fold up at night; closely related to yopo.

chachapoya-culture.name: Chachapoya
chachapoya-culture.summary: An Andean people called the 'Warriors of the Clouds' who lived in Peru's cloud forests, resisting Inca conquest before being absorbed into the Inca Empire shortly before the Spanish arrived.

ku-lap.name: Kuélap
ku-lap.summary: A walled settlement in the mountains of the Amazonas region of Peru, built by the Chachapoyas culture in the 6th century AD overlooking the Utcubamba Valley.

gran-pajat-n.name: Gran Pajatén
gran-pajat-n.summary: An archaeological site in Peru's Andean cloud forests, within Río Abiseo National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1990.

chiribaya-culture.name: Chiribaya culture
chiribaya-culture.summary: A culture that flourished along the coast of southern Peru and Chile from 700 CE until Spanish colonization, combining coastal fishing settlements with inland farming communities, notably studied in the Osmore valley.

osmore-river.name: Osmore River
osmore-river.summary: A river system in southern coastal Peru, rising in the Andes and known by different names along its course, whose valley holds archaeological sites spanning 10,000 years.

chimor.name: Chimor
chimor.summary: A pre-Inca kingdom of the Chimú culture on Peru's coast, arising about 900 CE and conquered by the Inca around 1470; Guacricur, grandson of its founder Taycanamo, expanded its rule over the lower valley.

moche-valley.name: Moche Valley
moche-valley.summary: A fertile valley in northern Peru around the Moche River, farmed since pre-Columbian times and now home to the city of Trujillo.

trujillo-peru.name: Trujillo, Peru
trujillo-peru.summary: A city on Peru's northwestern coast, site of the earlier Moche and Chimú cultures, later declared the provisional capital of Peru by Bolívar in 1824.

pikillaqta.name: Pikillaqta
pikillaqta.summary: A large Wari culture archaeological site near Cusco, Peru, occupied roughly 550 to 1100 AD and used mainly for ceremonies.
